Yesterday saw two pieces of news about next year's iPhone that contradict each other; this device, seen as the iPhone 20th anniversary commemorative model, is also regarded as the embodiment of Apple's long-standing vision of "a single sheet of glass."

Regarding what we can actually expect, there have been conflicting reports circulating for some time, but yesterday's divergence can be said to be the most dramatic so far……

The current situation

Former Apple design chief Jony Ive has often spoken about his long-term vision of eventually turning the iPhone into "a single sheet of glass"; even though Ive has left the company, there is still a widespread belief that Apple is moving in this direction.

Although Apple generally does not make a big fuss over anniversaries, the consensus is that they want to get as close as possible to realising this vision before the iPhone's 20th anniversary. This may include embedding Face ID under the display, and hiding the front camera beneath the screen.

However, we have already seen conflicting reports about these expectations. The initial view was that this would be a standalone model, similar to the iPhone Air and the upcoming iPhone Ultra, but more recent reports indicate that this design will appear on next year's iPhone Pro models.

In sequential terms, that would be the iPhone 19 Pro, but Apple might also choose to skip a generation and name it the iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary.

Yesterday's contradictory reports

Yesterday's situation became even more muddled when an analyst claimed that Apple had abandoned the idea of launching an all-glass iPhone next year.

But Bloomberg's Mark Gurman immediately refuted this claim.

The more likely reality

The key point is that Apple's vision for the iPhone does not have a single endpoint. What they plan to launch next year is just one step, or several steps, towards the sci-fi vision of "a single sheet of glass."

The question is not whether this goal can be achieved next year, but how far Apple will go in that direction. But whether it is one step or several, this is certainly not going to be the last step in the evolution of iPhone design.

In fact, Gurman revealed that Apple has actually backtracked on the goals previously expected for next year.

Analysts at Jefferies likely received the same information, but were a step behind and mistakenly assumed that the entire plan had been shelved.

My personal expectation is that next year's design will be a major leap forward — comparable to the breakthrough of the iPhone X — but there will be further developments in the years to come. For me, the biggest question is whether the 2027 iPhone will have a breakthrough large enough to warrant being marked in some special branding way, such as being labelled as the 20th anniversary iPhone (I think this is unlikely), being given a special name, or skipping a generation and being called the iPhone 20.

What are your expectations? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
